observable_outcome: The scheduler becomes a role a real caller can be, and the Runner's own path stops calling itself the owner. Measured at 76cfa91, no non-test code anywhere constructs an application.Caller with RoleScheduler: internal/api/auth.go produces only RoleRunner (:50, :85) and RoleOwner (:59, :99), and internal/runner/orchestrator.go:39 fabricates Caller{Role: RoleOwner, Subject: "runner-local-owner"} because it has no scheduler identity to use. Thirteen non-test sites ACCEPT the role and none requires it. The role is nevertheless kept, not dropped, on three measurements: contracts/openapi/openapi-v1.yaml:6-8 declares increment decomposition 'a loop scheduler responsibility'; a real identity already authenticates as the scheduler, the Cloud Scheduler OIDC service account cmd/control-plane requires as RECONCILE_IDENTITY and internal/api/api.go:87-92 verifies on POST /internal/reconcile; and internal/application/caller.go:64-72 makes RoleScheduler the SOLE producer of domain.ActorTypeLoop for a Requirement's, a Repository's and a Control Intent's requester, so removing it would make the domain's own owner-versus-loop distinction unreachable for all of them. The repair is one sanctioned producer, application.LoopCaller; one field on CombinedAuthenticator, SchedulerIdentity, checked before the owner map and refusing an identity configured as both; the reconcile branch carrying that caller on the context it already authorises, with its own check byte-unchanged; and the Orchestrator's fabricated caller replaced by an injected, fail-closed field. What fixes the outcome is an executed proof over the composed handler that the scheduler identity captures a Requirement whose requested_by.actor_type reads loop -- reachable for the first time -- is refused on every owner-only route, and is accepted on exactly the pairs that already name it. Nothing becomes scheduler-only and no contract changes.

A4. The producer. Document it as the ONLY sanctioned way to obtain a scheduler caller and as the in-process analogue of internal/api/auth.go's transport constructors. Add no other exported symbol, no field to Caller, and no new Role. Assert by a source scan that no package outside internal/application constructs a Caller literal with RoleScheduler, and that the count of non-test RoleScheduler PRODUCER sites is exactly one after this task -- so the repair is measured as 0 -> 1.

A5. The transport. Add one field, SchedulerIdentity string, to internal/api/CombinedAuthenticator. Authenticate keeps its existing order exactly: the runner-session header branch first and byte-unchanged; then parseIAPEmail; then, BEFORE the OwnerEmails lookup, if SchedulerIdentity is non-empty and its lowercased trimmed value equals the asserted email, return application.LoopCaller(email); then the existing owner branch, unchanged.
